summary: X uses OAuth 2.0 with mandatory PKCE. Recent 2026 changes shifted the platform to a pay-per-use model with no free tier for new developers, though authentication remains self-serve and doesn't require a manual review queue for standard production use.

verdict.why: Setup is self-serve with no app review, but X has no free tier: API access is pay-per-use with a card on file, and apps requesting DM or write scopes show users a 'sensitive permissions' warning that self-serve apps cannot remove.
verdict.approvalTrigger: No review for self-serve pay-per-use apps. Enterprise access is a separate sales process.
verdict.cost: Pay-per-use, card required (no free tier). Per-request prices vary by source; check the Developer Portal.

oauth.refreshTokens: Requires the offline.access scope; access tokens last 2 hours. Store the newest refresh token after every refresh.
oauth.redirectUriRules: Exact match required; case-sensitive; HTTPS required for production; http://localhost allowed.
oauth.scopeNotes: DM and write scopes (dm.read, tweet.write, ...) trigger a 'sensitive permissions' warning on the consent screen for pay-per-use apps (since 14 Sep 2026).

prerequisites.detail: Account must have a verified phone number and email address.
Pay-per-use billing requires a valid credit card on file for API credits.

steps.title: Create Developer Account
steps.detail: Log in to the Developer Portal with your verified X account and apply for the Pay-Per-Use plan.

steps.title: Configure User Authentication
steps.detail: In App Settings, enable 'User authentication'. Set App Type to 'Web App' and add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add to the Callback URIs.

steps.title: Obtain Credentials
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the 'Keys and Tokens' tab into your Composio configuration.

steps.title: Implement PKCE Flow
steps.detail: Generate code_verifier and code_challenge (S256). Exchange auth_code for tokens within 30 seconds of receipt.

steps.title: Add offline.access Scope
steps.detail: Include 'offline.access' in the scope list to ensure the agent can refresh the 2-hour access tokens.

blockers.howToUnblock: The code expires in 30 seconds. Ensure your backend handles the exchange immediately upon redirect.

blockers.blocker: 'Sensitive permissions' warning on the consent screen
blockers.howToUnblock: It cannot be removed for self-serve pay-per-use apps. Request only the scopes you need (Composio's defaults include dm.read, dm.write and tweet.write), explain the warning in your connect flow, or talk to X sales about Enterprise access.

gotchas: Refresh tokens are single-use; the agent must store the new refresh token returned with every refresh request.
Redirect URIs are character-sensitive; even a trailing slash mismatch will cause a 400 error.
The Free tier is discontinued; all API calls now incur metered costs.

agentCanDo: Estimate costs based on predicted read/write volume
youMustDo: Provide payment details for pay-per-use billing
Manually copy-paste Callback URIs into the portal

claims.claim: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE is mandatory for user-context access.
The authorization code must be exchanged within 30 seconds.
Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on every use.
claims.note: Review: the cited page (X Ads API MCP docs) is not the OAuth reference; not confirmed in the OAuth 2.0 docs.

claims.claim: A Free API tier is no longer available for new developers in 2026.
Pay-per-use apps requesting DM or write scopes show a 'sensitive permissions' warning on the consent screen (since 14 Sep 2026); it cannot be removed for self-serve apps.
claims.note: Announced by X on its developer forum.

claims.claim: The authorization code is valid for 30 seconds, and access tokens for 2 hours; offline.access is required for a refresh token.
claims.note: Checked in review against X's OAuth 2.0 docs.

openQuestions: The exact monthly cap for pay-per-use reads (sources vary between 2M and 3M).
Exact pay-per-use prices per post and per read (only third-party sources found).
Refresh-token lifetime (not stated in X's OAuth 2.0 docs).
Whether any path short of Enterprise removes the sensitive-permissions warning.
composioAdvice: Composio has no managed X app, so you must create your own in the X Developer Portal (pay-per-use, card required) and add Composio's redirect URI. Composio's default X scopes include dm.read, dm.write and tweet.write, which make X show your users a 'sensitive permissions' warning; trim the scopes to what your agent actually uses. Keep offline.access, or connections drop after 2 hours.

notes: Generated live on the production site (gemini-3-flash-preview after model failover, 17 tool calls, 77 s). The author also reviewed it against X's developer docs.
Confirmed by probe: PKCE is mandatory (the token endpoint rejects requests without code_verifier) and the discovery document at api.x.com advertises S256.
Confirmed against X's docs: 30-second authorization codes, 2-hour access tokens, offline.access required for refresh tokens.
Confirmed on X's developer forum: the Free tier is gone (pay-per-use only), and DM/write scopes show a sensitive-permissions warning since 14 Sep 2026.
Downgraded: specific per-request prices (third-party blog only) and a ~6-month refresh-token lifetime (not in X's docs) are now listed as not confirmed.
